title: Existing unbounded compact-support composition without compactness hypotheses
statement: Let $A$ be a finite commutative ring and $f:X\to Y$, $g:Y\to T$ morphisms of arbitrary schemes such that $f,g,gf$ admit factorizations as an open immersion followed by a proper morphism. Let $Rf_!$, $Rg_!$, and $R(gf)_!$ be open extension followed by derived proper direct image, using their chosen compactifications. Then there is a natural isomorphism $R(gf)_!\cong Rg_!Rf_!$ on the ordinary unbounded constant-$A$ module derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. No quasi-compactness assumption is needed. The scheme, morphism, and functor notions used here are those of [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-open-immersion].

source.place: nonempty_iso_rightDerivedLowerShriek_comp and preceding docstring, proof using graphs in the product of the proper ambients.

proof.text: Use the already-proved source composition theorem attached below. Its construction takes the product of the proper ambients of g and gf and embeds X as a closed subscheme of an open in that product. Over the open Y in the second ambient the same embedding computes Rf_!. Exchange proper direct image past the open extension, compose the proper direct images and the open extensions, and identify the compactification models. The source construction uses only the supplied compactifications; it does not require quasi-compactness or Noetherianity.
